description: AVG result typing, live-verified against Snowflake: fixed-point inputs (INTEGER or NUMBER(p,s)) yield a NUMBER whose scale is (max input scale) + 6, rounded HALF_UP with trailing zeros KEPT - AVG of the integers 90 and 95 is exactly 92.500000 and AVG(2, 2) renders 2.000000 rather than 2 - while any FLOAT input keeps the double average, whose rendering carries no scale-6 zeros. An empty input is NULL. Converted 1:1 from functions/AvgTypingTest (now retired); its assertInstanceOf(Double.class) type check is expressed here as the rendered form, since a fixed-point AVG renders 2.000000 where the double path renders 2 - the results are stringified with '<' || x || '>' so the trailing zeros are part of the assertion.

steps.sql: INSERT INTO dbls SELECT 1.5::DOUBLE UNION ALL SELECT 2.5::DOUBLE
